title: Nine broad-profile GJ667 exposures have two header-pointing directions after linear proper-motion correction
abstract: We test whether one pointing direction describes nine broad-profile GJ667 HARPS exposures from an earlier audit. We compare twelve original ESO headers with target positions after linear proper-motion correction. Seven broad exposures have northwest offsets and extreme SERVAL velocities. Two have northeast offsets, the largest profile widths, and small SERVAL shifts. The direction split holds under two RA proper-motion conventions and east boundaries from -5 to +5 arcseconds. Three selected narrow controls have smaller offsets. This shows that a single direction toward the bright binary does not describe all nine header anomalies. We do not identify the light in the fiber, prove two fault mechanisms, or find a new planet. Header frame effects, a small control sample, shared observations, and absent spectra limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact input hashes and retrieval steps are included. External raw data and per-exposure records remain outside the baseline package.
